Under the selected cohort organization, the model performs a single shared dense/MoE traversal and preserves normal KV-update semantics while executing attention in two context-compatible launches. Both cohorts execute within the same model iteration and together cover exactly the requests in 𝒟 ⁡ ( t ) \mathcal{D}(\text{t}) . Thus, execution admission changes the physical organization of attention without duplicating complete model execution or changing the participating request set. All requests remain in the iteration, and the remaining layer computation proceeds over the complete reordered batch. Dynamic reevaluation. At every eligible pure-decode iteration, Coda reconstructs 𝒟 ⁡ ( t ) \mathcal{D}(\text{t}) and reevaluates its materialized context composition. Session progress, request completion, and asynchronous tool returns may therefore change the preferred organization from one iteration to the next. Coda falls back to complete-population execution when the population is insufficiently heterogeneous, the execution shape is unsupported, or the predicted gain is insufficient. 5 System Design: The Coda Routing Layer For coding-agent serving with multiple workers, Coda introduces a routing layer that determines the worker assignment for each arriving request. The layer considers three complementary placement signals. ( i ) KV reuse captures the reusable session prefix available at each worker. ( ii ) Worker load captures the pressure created by active requests. ( iii ) Context-length compatibility captures how closely the arriving context matches each worker’s active decode population. Coda applies these signals hierarchically: it preserves useful KV affinity when load-safe and uses context-length compatibility to select among the remaining load-eligible workers ( Finding 8 ). Reuse- and load-aware placement. Coda adopts SMetric’s reuse- and load-aware policy [ 22 ] as its parent routing policy. A session’s first request initially selects a least-loaded worker. For a session continuation, the router prefers the worker with the largest actual local-prefix hit and preserves this affinity while the worker remains within the configured overload bound. This policy exploits the locality of long-lived coding-agent sessions while limiting load imbalance caused by asynchronous tool-return bursts. Compatibility-aware placement. When KV affinity does not determine the destination, Coda considers workers at the minimum load or one active request above that minimum, and selects among them according to context-length compatibility .
